findings.question: Q1
findings.finding: The rate path BAC's 'upper end of 6-8%' NII guide was built on (one 25bp hike in September, set 2026-07-14) has moved up: the Fed hiked to 4.00% on 2026-09-16, the 2-year went 4.26% (07-13) to 4.75% (10-08) and the curve now prices a December hike plus two in H1 2027; BAC's own 10-Q puts banking-book NII at +$0.8B per +100bp at the short end, and the peers that spoke after BAC confirm the transmission (JPM raised FY26 NII to ~$106.2B from $105.5B with NII ex-Markets +4.4% QoQ; H.8 deposits +1.6% and loans +1.8% QoQ), so BAC's Q4 NII guide (~$17B FTE) and 2027 framing are more likely to land above the 'upper end' the street holds than at it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII guide is the line: +1.82% on 2026-04-15 (guide raised to 6-8%), +1.88% on 2026-07-14 (upper end), -3.78% on 2026-01-14 when the 2026 NII guide (5-7%) fell short of hopes despite an EPS beat (fool.com 2026-01-14).
findings.why_not_priced: Anchoring on the company's guide and stale estimates: the latest BAC estimate found (JPM Securities, 2026-10-06) models NII 'up QoQ' at the upper end of 6-8% with no change for the curve, and the consensus Q3 NII of ~$16.55B FTE (beinsure, 2026-10-12) implies a Q4 near $16.95B, i.e. exactly 8%. The confirming peer data landed 2026-10-13, one session before the print, and BAC was down 1.1% intraday that session with KBWB (-1.2%, both at 13:48 ET) instead of trading up on JPM's raise. If priced, 2027 NII estimates would already sit above the July framing and BAC would have decoupled from the sector on JPM's raise.
findings.independence: BAC 10-Q Table 41 sensitivity (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/70858/000007085826000394/bac-20260630.htm, 2026-07-31, company document); FRED 2-year and fed funds series (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DGS2, read to 2026-10-08); H.8 deposits via FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DPSACBW027SBOG, week of 2026-09-30); JPM supplement NII ex-Markets $24,726M vs $23,677M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfex992supplement.htm). The JPM call and the JPM supplement share an issuer; the counterweight that reaches the size is the Q2 call's 'markets business is slightly liability sensitive' and JPM not being rewarded for its raise.

findings.question: Q2
findings.finding: The Q3 capital-markets consensus sits exactly on BAC's own 2026-09-14 pre-guide (IB ~$1.71B, -15% YoY; sales and trading ~flat at $5.4B per beinsure 2026-10-12), but the peers that reported on 2026-10-13 printed the quarter well above that environment: JPM IB +14% YoY (advisory +32%, ECM +7%, DCM +4%) and only -8% QoQ, GS IB $3.22B +21% YoY (-5% QoQ) with equities +72% on record prime financing, JPM markets +15% and Citi markets +6%; BAC needs about -20% QoQ in IB to print $1.71B, and in Q3 2025 it printed IB of $2.05B against $1.65B expected after a similarly cautious intra-quarter steer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +4.37% on 2025-10-15 when IB rose 43% to $2.05B vs $1.65B expected (bgov); -5.14% on 2026-09-14 (vs KBWB -1.89%) on the pre-guide itself, so the soft quarter is in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Anchoring on the company's pre-guide: consensus EPS was cut from $1.16-1.19 to $1.11 around the pre-guide and the line items (IB $1.71B, trading flat) are its midpoints; the JPM Securities model at those inputs gives $1.12. The contradicting peer prints are one session old. If the market held a beat, BAC would have outperformed the sector on 2026-10-13; it moved with it. Size is net of revenue-related compensation (JPM raised its FY expense outlook to $108.6B on the same day) and cut for a tape that sold every bank beat on 2026-10-13.
findings.independence: GS 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000886982/000088698226000529/a3q26gsearningsresultspr.htm, 2026-10-13, independent issuer); Citi markets +6% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/earnings-live-updates-big-banks-q3-earnings-115135687.html, 2026-10-13); BAC 2025 precedent (https://news.bgov.com/capital-markets/bofa-bankers-beat-estimates-as-dealmaking-boosts-earnings-2, 2025-10-15). Counterweight in the size: Moynihan said BAC is 'not as well positioned in some of the businesses that had more activity' and that prime financing slowed in international/Asia (https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_51f2a2df40344508fd98d4f74a5a35dd/bankofamerica/db/775/10600/webcast_transcript/2026-09-14+Barclays+Financial+Services+Conference_BAC_ADA.pdf).

findings.question: Q4
findings.finding: BAC's own securitised card book improved through the quarter: the BA Master Credit Card Trust II net charge-off rate was 2.13% in July and 2.15% in August against 2.23% in June and 2.39% in April, with 30+ day delinquencies flat at 1.26-1.28%; JPM's $539M build was 'just from new activity' and WFC's net charge-offs were $983M, so a clean consumer-led credit line (provision near Q2's $1.37B) is the likely answer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No credit surprise in the last four prints; Q2 2026 provision $1.37B and NCOs $1.4B were flat to Q1 and drew no comment in the +1.88% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Slow data the market underweights: monthly trust 10-D figures appear in no preview and no consensus provision is visible (beinsure 2026-10-12 gives none). Small because the trust is ~$14B of a much larger card book, commercial credit is the rest, and the bar is not set on credit.

findings.question: Q5
findings.finding: BAC's capital headroom for buybacks shrank in Q3: AOCI was -$12.0B at June 30 and the analyst expects -$15-16B after the rate rise (AOCI counts in BAC's CET1), the CET1 minimum is 10.0% through 2026 with the GSIB surcharge expected to rise on 2027-01-01 against an 11.2% ratio, the dividend went to $0.32 (+14%), and JPM cut its Q3 repurchases to $1.06B from $6.7B; on that arithmetic the Q3 buyback lands near $3-5B against $6.0B in Q2, at or below the street's 'could slow'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No BAC precedent in the last four prints; JPM was flat on 2026-10-13 after an 84% buyback cut that came with an NII raise and an EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the JPM Securities note (2026-10-06) says repurchases 'could slow from the Q2 pace of $6 billion' and puts AOCI at -$15-16B, but no estimate found quantifies the cut, and JPM's -84% sets a harsher reference than 'could slow'. Shrunk because Moynihan said 'we don't really feel any capital pressure to build' (2026-09-14) and JPM said its cut had 'nothing to do with AOCI'.
findings.independence: JPM supplement buyback $1,057M vs $6,703M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfex992supplement.htm, 2026-10-13); JPM Securities note (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/jpmorgan-reiterates-bank-of-america-stock-rating-on-nii-outlook-93CH-4933594, 2026-10-06); dividend 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/70858/000007085826000364/bac-20260723.htm, 2026-07-24); DeMare ranks buybacks fifth behind financial strength (https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_45bc8d3b7d1dfc677cb0c2500486fd1e/bankofamerica/db/775/10607/webcast_transcript/2026-09-23+BofA+Securities+Conference_BAC_ADA.pdf, 2026-09-23).

findings.why_not_priced: Not a mispricing claim: a symmetric macro event inside the window, filed at zero so the window's rate risk is on the record and reaches abs_move_pct.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the balanced skew (+0.26) and the call-heavy open interest; it leans against the -9.2% 20-day run-up only because a third of that drawdown is the company's own pre-guide (-5.1% on 2026-09-14), which the peer prints say was conservative.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Q2 fee finding was cut from +0.60 to +0.45 because every bank beat was sold on 2026-10-13. p_up was kept in the 55-60 band rather than raised.

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is an inference): the Q1 NII finding was trimmed from +0.60 to +0.50. It stays medium-sized because BAC's 10-Q quantifies the sensitivity, management said higher rates help, and JPM confirmed the effect by raising its NII guide.

Rule 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number): the Q5 buyback finding was cut from -0.30 to -0.20. The analyst already models a slowdown, Moynihan said 'no capital pressure', and JPM said its cut was not about AOCI.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): re-checked. Three sources after the revisions agree on $1.11 and the company guide anchors NII and fees, so no cap was applied.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest of 1.2% with 2.3 days to cover and skew of +0.26 were checked. Nothing conflicts with a long sign.

Rule 2 (name the line): each finding has a lands_on. The NII finding is guidance, the fee and credit findings are the reported quarter, the buyback finding is capital return, and the CPI finding is other. There are no one-offs.

Not a LESSONS change: after the LESSONS read, beinsure (2026-10-12) showed the consensus IB line is $1.71B, the pre-guide midpoint. On that evidence the Q2 finding was raised from +0.45 to +0.55 and p_up from 57 to 58.
Not a LESSONS change: a zero-sized CPI finding was added during the set review. It moves abs_move_pct, not the sum.
The 'what has worked' note (a peer's print after the company last spoke leaves consensus stale) describes the Q1 and Q2 findings. It argued against cutting them further.

key_questions.answer: Q3 FTE NII most likely lands in line, ~$16.5-16.65B against $16.55B (banking book +2.5-3.5% QoQ on day count, repricing and balances, Global Markets NII flat to slightly down after the hike). The outlook is where the answer differs from the priced one: the curve the July guide assumed (one September hike) has moved up 50-70bp at the short end, BAC's 10-Q says that is worth roughly +$0.4-0.5B of annual banking-book NII, and the peers that spoke after BAC raised or held NII with a steep Q4 step (JPM ex-Markets Q4 ~$25.5B vs $24.7B; WFC Q4 ~$13B vs $12.5B). So the likelier call is FY26 at or slightly above 8% with Q4 near $17.0B FTE and a 2027 framing helped by the curve, against a street still at 'upper end of 6-8%'. Offsets: Global Markets NII is liability sensitive, commercial deposits reprice, and JPM's raise bought nothing today.

premortem.other_way_reason: The stock fell on a quarter that was down sharply QoQ (EPS from $1.21, S&T from $7.2B) in a tape that sold every bank beat on 2026-10-13. BAC cut its Q3 buyback toward JPM's level as AOCI losses and the 2027 GSIB step-up squeezed CET1. The NII outlook was only reaffirmed at 'upper end' because the hike raised Global Markets funding and commercial deposit costs. A hot CPI at 8:30 ET pushed the 10-year back toward 5.3% and took the banks with it.
premortem.question: Q5
premortem.evidence_already_had: JPM's buyback cut to $1.06B; the analyst's AOCI estimate of -$15-16B; the 10-Q's CET1 minimum and the GSIB step-up; the Q2 call saying 'markets business is slightly liability sensitive'; the 2026-10-13 tape; the 2026-01-14 precedent (-3.78% on a beat with a soft NII guide); CPI timed at 8:30 ET.

investment_decision.reason: BAC reset its own bar on 2026-09-14 (-5.1% that day, EPS consensus cut to $1.11), and the consensus line items still sit on that pre-guide (IB $1.71B, trading flat). Every peer that reported after BAC spoke printed a better capital-markets quarter (Q2). The curve BAC's NII guide was built on has since moved 50-70bp higher, and JPM raised its NII guide on it (Q1). Credit looks clean on BAC's own card trust (Q4). Against that, the Q3 buyback is likely smaller (Q5) and the 2026-10-13 tape sold every bank beat, so the edge is real but small and the sign is a modest long.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: IB and sales and trading printing at or below the pre-guide midpoints ($1.7B, ~$5.35B), with the NII outlook left at 'upper end of 6-8%' and no 2027 framing, or a Q3 buyback cut to JPM-like levels (under $2B) with a lower Q4 signal.
